n: God answers “Where is the God of justice?”: He will send His messenger to prepare the way, then the Lord will suddenly come to His temple. Jesus identified John the Baptist as this messenger; the D&C applies it to the latter days too. The Savior quoted Malachi 3–4 to the Nephites.

f.w: shall suddenly come to his temple
Behold, I will send my messenger

n: But who can endure His coming? He is like a refiner’s fire that burns away impurities, and like a launderer’s strong soap that scrubs clean.

f.w: who may abide the day of his coming?

f.g: Strong lye soap used by fullers to whiten cloth.

n: Like a refiner patiently watching silver in the fire, He will purify the priests so they offer righteous offerings. Latter-day revelation connects this to the restoration of the priesthood and temple work.

f.w: he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver

n: Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the good old days.

f.w: as in the days of old

n: God will come near in judgment as a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, liars, those who cheat workers of their wages, and those who oppress widows, orphans, and foreigners.

f.w: oppress the hireling in his wages

n: “I am the Lord, I change not.” Because God is constant and faithful to His covenant, Jacob’s descendants have not been destroyed.
Ever since their ancestors’ days they have strayed from God’s ordinances. “Return to Me, and I will return to you.” But they ask, “How shall we return?”

f.w: Return unto me, and I will return unto you

n: Will a person rob God? Yet you rob Me. How? In tithes and offerings. Tithing means giving a tenth back to God, who gives us everything.

f.g: A tenth of one’s increase, given to God.

n: The whole nation is under a curse because of robbing God.

f.w: Ye are cursed with a curse

n: A famous promise: bring the full tithe to the storehouse so there is food in God’s house, and test Him — He will open the windows of heaven and pour out blessings beyond your capacity. One of the few places God invites us to “prove” Him.

f.w: open you the windows of heaven

n: God will stop the “devourer” — pests like locusts — so crops are not destroyed and vines don’t drop fruit too early.

f.g: Locusts or other pests destroying crops.

n: All nations will call them blessed, and the land will be delightful.
“Your words have been harsh against Me,” says the Lord. They ask, “What have we said?”
You’ve said, “Serving God is useless. What do we gain by obeying Him and walking around in mourning?”

f.w: It is vain to serve God

f.g: Going about in sackcloth — showing outward penitence.

n: “The arrogant are the happy ones; the wicked prosper and even test God and get away with it.” A common complaint when life seems unfair.

Then those who reverenced the Lord talked together, and He listened. A book of remembrance was written before Him for those who honored His name. God notices and records the faithful. Adam’s family kept a book of remembrance too.
“They will be Mine,” says the Lord, “My treasured possession on the day I act, and I will spare them as a father spares a son who serves him.”

f.g: Hebrew segullah — a special treasure, God’s own possession.

n: Then you will again see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between those who serve God and those who don’t. Justice will be visible.

f.w: discern between the righteous and the wicked
